conditions.engine: MuJoCo WebAssembly (@mujoco/mujoco) in Node, timestep 2 ms; probes in tests/measure/patch-probes.ts on tests/measure/gravity-harness.ts
conditions.request: chat.completions, response_format json_object, temperature left at the model default (not sent), no streaming; thinking off = chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking false; thinking on = default reasoning with max_tokens 4096 covering reasoning and answer; up to 2 retries on network errors, 429 and 5xx
conditions.loop: iteration 0 = the probe's naive program; on a fail the patcher gets the task, the world line, the knobs with bounds and meaning, one line per earlier attempt (knobs or patch, and the check line of its note) and the last failure note; its "set" is validated and clamped (patch-probes.ts applyPatch); at most 5 patches; a failed or unparseable call counts as a patch that changes nothing
conditions.world_line: the patcher is told the gravity; hand-off velocity, offsets and vehicle bursts reach it only through measurements in the failure note
conditions.expert_check: each case/seed also runs a hand-written expert program; a case whose expert fails is reported as unsolvable with these knobs
conditions.seeds: per arm, in each arm's config
conditions.round_2: arms named r2-*: the next patch prompt says when a requested value was clamped to a bound or rejected; escalation arms switch patcher after a no-op patch (re-asked at once) or after the base patcher's second failed patch; ledger script patch-loop-r2 with its own cap
conditions.liquid: pour-liquid: lib/sim/fluid.ts position-based liquid, 600 particles at 4 mm (38 mL), one-way coupled to the MuJoCo cups via lib/sim/fluid-mujoco.ts, 60 frames/s with the solver's defaults

rules.rule: In very low gravity (<0.1 g), lower the release height to contact the surface to avoid toppling of tall objects.
rules.evidence: place probe, Mars 0.05g (frame0.05g), 3 repairs (three seeds) where changing release_height_mm from 10 mm to 0 mm eliminated toppling.

rules.rule: Increase the tilt angle of the source cup to improve bead transfer when pouring.
rules.evidence: pour probe, Earth 1g and Mars 0.379g (nominal), 4 repairs (Earth seed2, Mars seeds1‑3) where raising tilt_deg from 90° to 100° cleared beads left in the source.

rules.rule: Lengthen the tilt duration to allow more beads to flow out of the source cup.
rules.evidence: pour probe, Earth 1g (nominal) 1 repair (seed3) and Mars 0.379g (nominal) 3 repairs (seeds1‑3) where increasing tilt_s (Earth 3→4 s, Mars 1→1.5‑2 s) removed residual beads.

rules.rule: When the target is offset laterally, use a hold‑and‑wait strategy instead of a quick pour to ensure complete transfer.
rules.evidence: pour probe, Earth 1g (target+30mm) 3 repairs (seeds1‑3) and Mars 0.379g (target+30mm) 1 repair (seed3) where switching strategy from 'pour' to 'hold-and-wait' cleared beads left despite a +30 mm offset.

rules.rule: When placing an object while the vehicle accelerates horizontally, set the release height to zero (or as low as possible) so the object contacts the surface immediately upon release.
rules.evidence: place; Earth 1g & Mars 0.379g; vehicle accel 0.2g along +x; defaults failed (toppled); succeeded after setting release_height_mm=0 in 5,4,3,3 repairs respectively.

rules.rule: When placing under horizontal acceleration, reduce the release speed to ≤5 mm/s and add a dwell time of ≥2 s before opening the gripper to let the object settle.
rules.evidence: place; Earth 1g & Mars 0.379g; vehicle accel 0.2g along +x; defaults failed; succeeded after release_speed_mm_s=5 and wait_before_release_s=2 in the same 5,4,3,3 repairs.

rules.rule: For low horizontal acceleration (≤0.05 g) only zero release height is needed; speed and wait can stay at default.
rules.evidence: place; Mars 0.379g; vehicle accel 0.05g along +x; defaults failed; succeeded after release_height_mm=0 alone in three separate instances (1 repair each).

rules.rule: To pour successfully, increase the tilt angle beyond the default (≥100°) and/or lengthen the tilt duration to evacuate the source.
rules.evidence: pour; Earth 1g & Mars 0.379g; no disturbance; defaults failed (beads left); succeeded after tilt_deg=100 and tilt_s=1.5–4 s in repairs counts 3,4,2,2,3.

rules.rule: Shift the source cup toward the target (+x) by 10–40 mm to compensate for bead trajectory during pouring.
rules.evidence: pour; Earth 1g & Mars 0.379g; no disturbance; defaults failed; succeeded after target_offset_mm=10 (no offset) or 40 (when target displaced) in repairs counts 3,4,2,2,3 and 4,5,5,4 respectively.

rules.rule: When the target is displaced ≥30 mm, use the hold‑and‑wait strategy after tilting to allow beads to settle before returning upright.
rules.evidence: pour; Earth 1g & Mars 0.379g; target cup +30 mm; defaults failed; succeeded after strategy=hold‑and‑wait, tilt_s=2, target_offset_mm=40 in repairs counts 4,5,5,4.

rules.rule: Under lower gravity (Mars ≈0.38 g) less tilt time is needed than on Earth while keeping the increased angle.
rules.evidence: pour; Mars 0.379g; no disturbance; defaults failed; succeeded with tilt_s=1.5–2 s (vs Earth 2–4 s) and tilt_deg=100 in repairs counts 2,2,3.

rules.rule: When the robot experiences horizontal acceleration while placing an upright object, set the release height to the surface (release_height_mm = 0), reduce the release speed to a low value (≈5 mm/s), and add a dwell time before opening the gripper (wait_before_release_s ≈ 2 s) to let the object settle.
rules.evidence: 8 place repairs (Earth 1 g and Mars 0.379 g, with vehicle accelerations of 0.05 g–0.2 g) succeeded after setting release_height_mm=0, release_speed_mm_s≈5 mm/s, wait_before_release_s≈2 s.

rules.rule: When pouring beads, increase the tilt angle beyond the nominal 90° (to about 100°), lengthen the tilt duration (tilt_s ≥ 1.5 s, up to ~4 s depending on conditions), shift the source forward along the pour direction (target_offset_mm > 0) to compensate for distance, and use a hold‑and‑wait strategy if the target is displaced farther than nominal.
rules.evidence: 9 pour repairs (Earth 1 g and Mars 0.379 g, with and without a 30 mm target offset) succeeded after increasing tilt_deg to ~100°, raising tilt_s to 1.5‑4 s, adding target_offset_mm of 10‑40 mm, and using hold‑and‑wait when the target was farther.

rules.rule: When the robot experiences horizontal acceleration while placing an upright object, set the release height to the surface (release_height_mm = 0), reduce the release speed to a low value (≈5 mm/s), and add a dwell time before opening the gripper (wait_before_release_s ≈ 2 s) to let the object settle.
rules.evidence: 8 place repairs (Earth 1 g and Mars 0.379 g, with vehicle accelerations of 0.05 g–0.2 g) succeeded after setting release_height_mm=0, release_speed_mm_s≈5 mm/s, wait_before_release_s≈2 s.

rules.rule: When pouring beads, increase the tilt angle beyond the nominal 90° (to about 100°), lengthen the tilt duration (tilt_s ≥ 1.5 s, up to ~4 s depending on conditions), shift the source forward along the pour direction (target_offset_mm > 0) to compensate for distance, and use a hold‑and‑wait strategy if the target is displaced farther than nominal.
rules.evidence: 9 pour repairs (Earth 1 g and Mars 0.379 g, with and without a 30 mm target offset) succeeded after increasing tilt_deg to ~100°, raising tilt_s to 1.5‑4 s, adding target_offset_mm of 10‑40 mm, and using hold‑and‑wait when the target was farther.

rules.rule: When placing an object while the vehicle accelerates horizontally, set the release height to zero (or as low as possible) so the object contacts the surface immediately upon release.
rules.evidence: place; Earth 1g & Mars 0.379g; vehicle accel 0.2g along +x; defaults failed (toppled); succeeded after setting release_height_mm=0 in 5,4,3,3 repairs respectively.

rules.rule: When placing under horizontal acceleration, reduce the release speed to ≤5 mm/s and add a dwell time of ≥2 s before opening the gripper to let the object settle.
rules.evidence: place; Earth 1g & Mars 0.379g; vehicle accel 0.2g along +x; defaults failed; succeeded after release_speed_mm_s=5 and wait_before_release_s=2 in the same 5,4,3,3 repairs.

rules.rule: For low horizontal acceleration (≤0.05 g) only zero release height is needed; speed and wait can stay at default.
rules.evidence: place; Mars 0.379g; vehicle accel 0.05g along +x; defaults failed; succeeded after release_height_mm=0 alone in three separate instances (1 repair each).

rules.rule: To pour successfully, increase the tilt angle beyond the default (≥100°) and/or lengthen the tilt duration to evacuate the source.
rules.evidence: pour; Earth 1g & Mars 0.379g; no disturbance; defaults failed (beads left); succeeded after tilt_deg=100 and tilt_s=1.5–4 s in repairs counts 3,4,2,2,3.

rules.rule: Shift the source cup toward the target (+x) by 10–40 mm to compensate for bead trajectory during pouring.
rules.evidence: pour; Earth 1g & Mars 0.379g; no disturbance; defaults failed; succeeded after target_offset_mm=10 (no offset) or 40 (when target displaced) in repairs counts 3,4,2,2,3 and 4,5,5,4 respectively.

rules.rule: When the target is displaced ≥30 mm, use the hold‑and‑wait strategy after tilting to allow beads to settle before returning upright.
rules.evidence: pour; Earth 1g & Mars 0.379g; target cup +30 mm; defaults failed; succeeded after strategy=hold‑and‑wait, tilt_s=2, target_offset_mm=40 in repairs counts 4,5,5,4.

rules.rule: Under lower gravity (Mars ≈0.38 g) less tilt time is needed than on Earth while keeping the increased angle.
rules.evidence: pour; Mars 0.379g; no disturbance; defaults failed; succeeded with tilt_s=1.5–2 s (vs Earth 2–4 s) and tilt_deg=100 in repairs counts 2,2,3.

rules.rule: When the robot experiences horizontal acceleration while placing an upright object, set the release height to the surface (release_height_mm = 0), reduce the release speed to a low value (≈5 mm/s), and add a dwell time before opening the gripper (wait_before_release_s ≈ 2 s) to let the object settle.
rules.evidence: 8 place repairs (Earth 1 g and Mars 0.379 g, with vehicle accelerations of 0.05 g–0.2 g) succeeded after setting release_height_mm=0, release_speed_mm_s≈5 mm/s, wait_before_release_s≈2 s.

rules.rule: When pouring beads, increase the tilt angle beyond the nominal 90° (to about 100°), lengthen the tilt duration (tilt_s ≥ 1.5 s, up to ~4 s depending on conditions), shift the source forward along the pour direction (target_offset_mm > 0) to compensate for distance, and use a hold‑and‑wait strategy if the target is displaced farther than nominal.
rules.evidence: 9 pour repairs (Earth 1 g and Mars 0.379 g, with and without a 30 mm target offset) succeeded after increasing tilt_deg to ~100°, raising tilt_s to 1.5‑4 s, adding target_offset_mm of 10‑40 mm, and using hold‑and‑wait when the target was farther.
